statement_summary: Security and Privacy Lead designated in writing
Annual risk assessment (SP 800-30) and targeted risk analyses
Risk acceptance authority; High risks never accepted
Sanctions; good-faith reporting protected
PCI DSS scope per account and channel; evidence for every SAQ answer
Service provider list, agreements with breach notice, yearly AOC check
Annual independent assessment
Total price in every ticket price display; accurate fee names and privacy notice
Annual policy review, acknowledgment, 5-year security records
Change control for website, ticketing, payment, and firewall settings
Approved script list for pages hosting the checkout widget; weekly page check; change alerts
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Named accounts; no shared door, website, or mailbox logins
Least privilege; at most 2 ticketing administrators; export and refund rights limited
MFA on every ticketing, website, suite, and administrator login, including MSP-held
Last-day checklist; shared secrets changed; season end for door logins
Monthly account check of ticketing users and tokens, website users, and suite users
API tokens with owner, purpose, narrow access, and end date
Named MSP and vendor accounts with MFA; yearly technician list
Separate staff network; crew Wi-Fi internet-only; Wi-Fi passwords changed each season
12-character passwords; none written at the door; no vendor defaults
10-minute computer lock; passcode and 5-minute lock on door tablets
Company systems for company work; look up only patrons you serve
Never take a card number by phone, email, chat, or paper; delete any that arrives
No patron or card data in personal accounts or public AI tools
Lock screens; never share passwords or MFA codes
Training at hire and yearly; phishing simulations; season reader briefing for contractor leads
Report suspected incidents at once
Signed policy acknowledgment
Ticketing channel breach runbook kept and printed
Report suspected incidents within 1 hour, including contractors
Log every incident
Weekly log check; monthly ticketing audit log export kept 12 months
Acquirer notice within 24 hours of suspected card compromise; card brand instructions
Insurer hotline first; MSP engaged
Suspicion and determination times recorded; notices per the P08 matrix with counsel
Capture evidence before deleting scripts, accounts, or tokens
Ransom or extortion payment only with approvals and an OFAC check
Vendor incident reports handled; 72-hour notice terms at renewal
Annual tabletop with the MSP and insurer hotline
Lessons learned within 30 days
Three classification levels
No card data kept in any form; delete or shred the same day
Patron records only in approved places; exports deleted within 30 days
Full-disk encryption on computers; encryption in transit
Inventory of devices, readers, SaaS, tokens, scripts, and Restricted data
Pre-show card reader inspection; spares locked
Approved AI tools only; P10 review before new AI or patron data uses
Backup of all mailboxes and files; MFA on the console; quarterly restore test
Retention periods and certified disposal
